readings: 'MDMA ... approved by the FDA' = FDA approval of midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD, the only MDMA program the forecaster's organization was pursuing on the statement date.

records.deadline_text: which we hope may happen in the middle of 2024
records.stage_note: Phase 3 program (MAPP1, MAPP2) complete on the statement date; the quote does not say whether the NDA had been submitted, so the phase 3 class applies.
records.note: Split -a of a compound claim (MDMA and psilocybin). 'The middle of 2024' is not an H1, quarter or month pattern; the year rule gives 31 December 2024. The FDA decides; the forecaster was a Lykos founder and board member on the statement date (affiliation to 2024-08-31), so affiliated true.

readings: No sponsor or indication is named, so the first FDA approval of any psilocybin drug product counts.

records.deadline_text: maybe near the end of 2025, 2026 potentially
records.phrase: I think, will be approved maybe
records.stage_note: At least one psilocybin program (COMP360, Compass Pathways) was in Phase 3 on the statement date; the forecaster names no sponsor.
records.note: Split -b of a compound claim. The clause 'once MDMA, if it becomes approved by the FDA' makes the psilocybin claim conditional on E-0001, which the FDA decides. The later of the two named years (2026) sets the deadline. 'Will' is the strongest phrase in the sentence and sets bin A; 'maybe' qualifies the timing, not the approval. The forecaster holds no disclosed role in a psilocybin sponsor.

A count of people treated with MDMA-assisted therapy by 2032 has no named public series that could resolve it; the quantity template requires one and the forecaster gives none. 'We've had some estimates that we will hopefully treat' also cites an internal estimate rather than stating an expectation.

Conditional on 'if we can get the research on ibogaine ... fully funded': the condition is the forecaster's own organization (MAPS, its Open Ibogaine project) raising money and running the program, which the forecaster controls. Under the intake rule a condition under the forecaster's control is rejected as CONTROL. The claim is also undated and 'could'.

readings: 'FDA approval' after 'they'll come to an agreement' = FDA approval of midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD on any review cycle; the agreement with the FDA is not itself the event.

records.stage_note: Post-CRL: the August 2024 complete response letter and the October 2024 FDA meeting are public on the statement date; a further Phase 3 study is required.
records.note: 'Three years from now' = statement date plus 3 years. 'Will be very likely' reads as 'very likely' (bin B); 'will' is the auxiliary of 'likely', not an assertion phrase. The Lykos affiliation ended 2024-08-31, before the statement date, and MAPS is not an alias of an entity named in the event, so affiliated false.

A delay estimate ('could delay approval for another three and a half years or so') gives no proposition that resolves TRUE or FALSE: the words set neither a date by which approval occurs nor a date before which it does not, and 'or so' has no band. Writing either would invent a threshold.
